texts: The records track thread weight, sea-water source, boil time, and vessel yield.
Hesper consults the records for seasonal planning.
One apprentice serves at Cauldron Hall each season.
Jeb served at Cauldron Hall in the autumn of Year 1.
Coraline Ash served at Cauldron Hall briefly in the winter of Year 1.

review.notes: The multi-word name stays one opaque symbol with exactly one Name atom and no modifier genus (no cauldron), while the kind word inside the name licenses (Member cauldron_hall hall); keep takes Agent/Theme (not Holder — it is not own/have/lack), the habitual present correctly carries no status atom, and distillation_record is a licensed bare kind-level object with its noun-modifier genus suppressed.

fields.sentence: The records track thread weight, sea-water source, boil time, and vessel yield.

q1_issues.issue: The four coordinated objects are stacked as four Theme atoms on one track event, but coordinated noun phrases are distributive by default and the whole predication should be replicated once per conjunct; multiple same-role atoms on a single event are licensed only for the collective (multiple-Agent) reading, which 'track' does not trigger.

The definite plural 'the records' gets the group witness and group event but no per-member distribution rule over (PartOf $x sk_group_1), which a grouped plural with a distributive predicate requires ('track' is not one of the collective predicates, though the collective reading is arguable here).

review.notes: Compound handling is right on all four objects (head genus emitted, noun modifiers unexposed), the bare kind fillers fit the non-specific habitual clause, and the inanimate transitive subject correctly stays Agent. Every worked coordination example in the instruction set coordinates subjects, so the expansion of a four-item object list rests on the general distributive rule alone.

issues.reason: Coordination & plurals states, with no restriction to subject position, that coordinated noun phrases are distributive by default — "replicate the whole predication once per conjunct (verbal -> one event each)" — and the one-event-many-fillers form is licensed only for reciprocal/aggregate predicates or an explicit "together / jointly", neither of which track supplies.

The half that stands: a grouped plural with a distributive predicate "also hands the predication to the group's members via a rule", and only a collective predicate (gather / meet / assemble) stays group-only, so the (PartOf $x sk_group_1) rule is missing; the half that is overstated: every worked distributive example is eventive (bark, pass, arrive), and a stative transitive over a definite plural has no precedent settling that each record separately tracks all four fields.

new_gaps: two distributions composing — a coordinated OBJECT list under an already-distributed grouped-plural subject — has no worked case: doctrine as written would demand four group events plus four per-member rules, and nothing states whether the object list still distributes once the subject rule has been minted
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form is four track events, one per coordinated object, each with (Agent $e sk_group_1) and a single Theme (the four genus atoms emitted once), and — for the distributive reading — a per-member (Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) (And (Member (sk_track $x) track) (Agent (sk_track $x) $x) (Theme (sk_track $x) <item>))) rule alongside each.
adjudication.notes: Compound handling is right on all four objects (head genus emitted, noun modifiers unexposed), the bare kind fillers fit the non-specific habitual objects, the inanimate transitive subject correctly stays Agent, and no status atom on the habitual present is correct.

fields.sentence: Hesper consults the records for seasonal planning.

review.notes: Definite plural "the records" correctly takes a group witness rather than Inheritance, "consults" is an Agent/Theme event with no status atom (habitual present), and the non-benefit "for" goes to the preposition-named oblique (For ...) rather than Beneficiary, with the bare abstract complement staying a constant. The seasonal_planning fusion with genus plus modifier genus is licensed since "seasonal" is an adjective that survives the predication test and is kept in its derived form.

fields.sentence: One apprentice serves at Cauldron Hall each season.

q2_gaps: a habitual / frequency clause whose participant varies per occurrence ('one apprentice serves ... each season') — the flat Every habitual form fixes the subject to one witness, and the occurrence-rule ('every time / whenever') route is explicitly reserved for occurrence domains rather than calendar periods, so a different apprentice per season has no carrier
a singular numeral determiner ('one apprentice') — Cardinality is defined only over a group, so an explicit count on a singular NP has no slot
review.notes: Location on the event (not LocatedIn), the Name plus separate kind atom for 'Cauldron Hall', and the status-free habitual all follow the instruction set. As emitted the parse reads as one fixed apprentice serving each season.

fields.sentence: Jeb served at Cauldron Hall in the autumn of Year 1.

q2_gaps: a NON-deictic season as a calendar granularity ('the autumn of Year 1'): the structured-term list has no Season constructor and the instruction set covers seasons only as speech-anchored deictic constants (last_spring / next_summer), so composing a bare `autumn` symbol with (Year 1) is an unguided extension of the day-part composition rule
review.notes: Name, Agent on the intransitive volitional subject, event-side Location for 'at Cauldron Hall' (not LocatedIn), the kind-word-inside-the-name type atom with no modifier genus, Past, and the (Year 1) term all follow the instruction set.

fields.sentence: Coraline Ash served at Cauldron Hall briefly in the winter of Year 1.

q2_gaps: A non-deictic season as a time value ('in the winter of Year 1'): the Time term constructors are Year/Month/Day/Weekday/Hour/Minute, bare symbols cover day-parts and DEICTIC seasons ('last_spring'), but nothing states how a plain season is encoded or how it composes with a stated year.
review.notes: 'briefly' correctly takes `(Duration <event> briefly)` rather than Manner, 'Cauldron Hall' follows the Kestrel-River pattern (one name symbol + separate `hall` type atom), and no kind atom is invented for Coraline Ash.
